title: Return an Optional for a result that may be absent

blocks.text: When a method may have no result, returning `Optional` says so in its type, and the caller cannot forget the empty case the way it can forget a `null` check. The method also validates its own parameters instead of failing on a `null`.

items: it returns the longest string: `longest(List.of("a", "abc", "ab"))` is `Optional.of("abc")`;
when several are equally long, the first of them wins: `longest(List.of("one", "two", "six"))` is `Optional.of("one")`;
an empty list, a list of only `null`s, and a `null` list give `Optional.empty()`.

cases.says: The longest of several strings is returned.
Of "one", "two" and "six", the first is returned.
null elements are skipped, not dereferenced.
An empty list and a null list give Optional.empty().

concepts: A result that may be absent is returned as an Optional, and a null parameter is validated rather than dereferenced.
